summary.text: Chelsey Hockett, a Democratic mother of two and community organizer who describes herself as not a career politician, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Texas's 5th Congressional District to Lance Gooden.
She has worked in restaurants and for airlines and has been involved with the Kaufman County Democratic Party.

paragraphs.text: Hockett was born in Frederick, Maryland, where she says she lived as a child, and attended Marcus High School. She earned a bachelor's degree from Texas Woman's University in 2015.

Her career experience includes working in restaurants, for airlines, and as a stay-at-home parent. In her Ballotpedia survey she says her first job, at age 15, was as a rescue technician at a veterinary clinic.
According to her campaign website, Hockett lives in Terrell, Texas, is a mother of two, and comes from a union family.
She has been affiliated with the Kaufman County Democratic Party, and her campaign website describes her organizing with friends, working with local Democrats, speaking at meetings and protesting.
Hockett advanced to a Democratic primary runoff after the March 3, 2026 primary and won the May 26, 2026 runoff over Ruth Torres. She describes herself as not a career politician.
During the campaign, she emphasized health care, public schools, labor and reproductive rights.
She received 48.5% of the vote to Lance Gooden's 51.5%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
